correctness.rationale: Counting edge incidences gives \(4F=2E_{\mathrm{int}}+B\), so the boundary length \(B\) is even. All bounded faces are quadrilaterals and the outer facial walk is even, hence the connected plane mesh graph is bipartite. In every cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary; because opposite vertices have the same bipartition color, each tile contributes exactly \(\pi\) angle mass to each color. Summing by vertices gives \(F\pi=2\pi I_C+\sum_{v\in\partial,C}\theta_v\) for either color, and subtraction yields the stated boundary-angle balance. For a square each color has \(B/2\) boundary vertices; if \(m_C\) of the four corners have that color, its boundary angle sum is \(B\pi/2-m_C\pi/2\), forcing \(m_C\) even. Walking around the four sides shows that exactly two adjacent odd side-subdivision counts would color the four corners in a \(3\)-to-\(1\) split, contradiction.
residual_risks: The graph argument assumes the stated finite edge-to-edge disk cellulation; it does not extend verbatim to non-edge-to-edge or non-simply-connected meshes.
